high.title: Braskem (BRKM5) Leads Ibovespa Gains and CSAN3 is Worst Performing Stock; See the Week's Highlights
high.summary: The Ibovespa extended its losing streak to five consecutive weeks amid uncertainties over Middle East conflicts and domestic political risks. Brazil's main stock index accumulated a 3.71% loss for the week, closing at 177,283.83 points. The USD/BRL spot rate finished at R$ 5.0678, up 1.63% on the day and 3.55% for the week. Political noise dominated investor attention during earnings season's final stretch. On Wednesday (13th), markets reacted to leaked audio of Senator and presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro discussing with Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro about a potential US$ 24 million transfer (approximately R$ 134 million). This political uncertainty, combined with geopolitical tensions, pressured Brazilian assets significantly, with the real weakening substantially against the dollar as risk-off sentiment prevailed.

high.title: Treasury Direct: Rates Decline with External Improvement and Domestic Scenario on Radar
high.summary: Brazilian government bond rates showed mixed performance on Monday (18th) after last week's sharp curve steepening, with geopolitics still in focus alongside the Focus Report and IBC-Br data. Fixed-rate bonds declined slightly while inflation-linked papers remained pressured in longer maturities, reflecting continued market caution about external scenarios and domestic risks. The partial relief in fixed-rate bonds came after recent rate escalation, as investors appeared to lock in returns at higher levels. However, rates remain near yearly highs as markets monitor international developments. Externally, focus was on Tasnim agency news that the US accepted suspending oil sanctions against Iran, signaling temporary flexibility on Iranian commodity restrictions that could ease oil prices and reduce inflationary pressures globally.

high.title: Ibovespa Opens Lower After IBC-Br and Petrobras (PETR4) Drop; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (18)
high.summary: The Ibovespa started the week with declines, diverging from overseas markets that operated mostly higher after oil prices turned negative. Petrobras (PETR4) fell over 1%, following the commodity's movement. Around 10:16 AM (Brasília time), Brazil's main stock index operated down 0.44% at 176,500.80 points. The spot dollar weakened against the real, following the currency's overseas performance, declining to R$ 5.0168 (-1.01%), while the DXY fell 0.25% to 99.035 points. The Central Bank's Economic Activity Index (IBC-Br), considered a GDP proxy, showed a 0.7% monthly decline in March (seasonally adjusted) - the first monthly drop this year and the steepest since May 2025, worse than market expectations. This economic activity contraction adds to concerns about Brazil's growth trajectory and monetary policy outlook.

medium.title: Wall Street Opens Slightly Higher with Expectations of US-Iran Negotiation Progress and Falling Oil Prices
medium.summary: US stock indices began Monday's session positively with US-Iran negotiations in focus. Trump threatened new attacks against Iran over the weekend, but Pakistan mediated a new Iranian proposal to the US. Tasnim agency reported US acceptance of suspending oil sanctions against Iran, providing temporary relief and potentially easing oil prices, which benefits emerging market currencies like the BRL through reduced inflationary pressures.

medium.title: Survey Points to Favorite Agribusiness Stocks in May; See Which Leads
medium.summary: Cosan (CSAN3) leads as the favorite agribusiness stock in May according to Money Times survey, receiving three recommendations among 17 analyzed portfolios. Suzano (SUZB3) and Klabin (KLBN11) tied for second place. The main driver for Cosan was debt reduction expectations and operational improvements at Raízen, though sugar/ethanol price volatility and climate risks remain concerns.
